subject: Taxes
title: Scotland's War of Independence
description: Learn Scotland's War of Independence in one minute.

hook.text: Edward I taxed Scotland to fund wars against France.

buildup.text: England treated Scotland as a revenue source. Tax collectors were English-appointed, and revenue flowed south to London.

discovery.text: William Wallace's rebellion in 1297 was partly a tax revolt. Scotland refused to fund English wars with Scottish money.

twist.text: Robert the Bruce won independence in 1328. Scotland's own parliament then taxed its people—but at least by consent.

climax.text: Scotland fought not against taxation but against taxation without representation. Self-rule meant self-taxation.

punchline.text: Not against taxes—against English taxes. Scotland fought for consent.

quiz.question: What was Scotland's core grievance about English taxation?
options: Taxes were levied without Scottish consent
